note: Pattern → action rules from prior engagements, anonymised. The provisioning flow reads this. Add a rule after every engagement; never add names or financials.

rules.pattern: Leadership cannot say what specific number or moment made them bring SPEC in now.
rules.action: Treat as a readiness signal. Slow the rollout; start with the organisational diagnostic and the covenant before any scoring.

rules.pattern: The business feels confident only after quarterly reconciliation; monthly numbers are not trusted.
rules.action: Make monthly, then weekly, financial visibility the first Earnings deliverable. Add the STAR rating to the commercial role.

rules.pattern: Two managers each cover about half of one role instead of one person owning it.
rules.action: Split into clearly owned streams (Commercial / Operations / Growth). Give each a head-of-department role and set their KPIs in the first week.

rules.pattern: Managers and consultants absorb admin work well below their pay level; system rollouts stall.
rules.action: Resource admin capacity first. It unblocks the systems rollout and every manager simultaneously.

rules.pattern: The business bought external marketing before fixing operational leadership.
rules.action: Sequence: operational ownership and business-development leadership first, external spend second. Quantify the misallocated spend as the cost-neutral case for SPEC.

rules.pattern: Gross profit target proposed by the GM is above what the operations head believes is achievable.
rules.action: Negotiate and lock a number both accept; record the proposed and agreed figures. A lower agreed target beats an imposed one.

rules.pattern: Not enough data to know what a conversion ratio should be.
rules.action: Keep the existing figure as a placeholder, flag it as unvalidated, and segment by sector before using it as an early-warning lever.

rules.pattern: Overtime proposed as a financial lever because fixed overhead is already covered.
rules.action: Treat as a masked understaffing signal. It works against Safety and People; cap utilisation targets at about 85%.

rules.pattern: Safety KPIs vary by role.
rules.action: Mirror the organisational standard (zero incidents, zero workers comp claims) into every role at supervisor level and above.

rules.pattern: Financial reporting blends what each person controls.
rules.action: Three standing reports: operational EBITDA (operations, excludes management salaries), controllable cash net profit (GM, before depreciation/interest/one-offs), full statutory (owner/board).

rules.pattern: Meetings are scattered and problem-focused.
rules.action: One weekly solutions meeting (SOG/COGS). Renaming it to something solutions-focused changed behaviour on its own.

rules.pattern: Weekly reports arrive as commentary with no fix.
rules.action: Every report of a miss must carry a proposed solution. Reject commentary-only submissions.

rules.pattern: The measurement system is built but nobody has entered data; dashboards show zeros.
rules.action: Never present an empty template as a result. Call the month a baseline, list what must be entered, and name who enters it.

rules.pattern: Two copies of the same log appear; entries are lost.
rules.action: One canonical log per tenant, append-only. The system, not a person, owns the file.

rules.pattern: Staff are wary about what scoring means for them personally.
rules.action: Walk each person through their scorecard face to face. Explain it scores the role's expectations, not the person.

rules.pattern: A capable person is doing work outside their lane and becoming negative.
rules.action: Give them clarity on their own lane through their role's KPIs before judging attitude.

rules.pattern: Owner wants a better business but refuses to fix an identified problem because it would upset people.
rules.action: Name it as the known failure shape (control reflex / avoidance). Return to the covenant. If it persists, the engagement is at risk — say so.

rules.pattern: Financial impact of prior wrong decisions surfaces during the engagement and looks like the consultant's fault.
rules.action: Set the J-curve expectation in week one and document the baseline so the cost of fixing accumulated decisions is visible as such.

rules.pattern: Owner becomes protective of SPEC when a competitor's trainer asks about it.
rules.action: That is the desired reaction. Describe SPEC publicly only in generic terms; give nothing proprietary away.

rules.pattern: Forty staff, only ten need to write.
rules.action: Full access for supervisor and above; read-only checklist view for everyone else. No seats for read-only users.
